leading_positions.synthesis: Seven of eleven round-1 files explicitly prefer B048 as the single prize part, with identical laureates (Marc J. Melitz, Elhanan Helpman). Boppart dropped Redding from his opening configuration; Andersson, Boppart, Fredriksson and Hjalmarsson state that they moved to B048 from another first choice. Shared reasoning: Melitz (2003) is the identifiable originating model, Helpman is the natural second name through the exporting-versus-FDI work, and more than twenty years of firm-level testing have supported the qualitative predictions (selection into exporting, exporter premia, within-industry reallocation). Several members also say it is distinct from the 2008 new-trade-theory prize. Not shared: citation wording differs (most are mechanism-focused; Fredriksson's also stresses linking firm-level data to aggregate outcomes). The members' alternatives also differ: B001 for six of the seven, B015 for four, B049 for two (Andersson, Enflo) and B037 for two (Dreber, Teorell). Every B048 supporter lists Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum (outside the ballot entry) as the main attribution risk. Functional-form dependence (e.g. Pareto productivity) of the welfare gains is also noted. This is a count of stated round-1 preferences, not a vote or ruling.

Three files explicitly prefer B001 with the same three laureates (Andrei Shleifer, Rafael La Porta, Florencio Lopez-de-Silanes). All three list B048 as an alternative (Strömberg also lists B049, Friberg B015, Hassler B037). All three accept that excluding Vishny is a real attribution cost and that the legal-origins causal claim and the coding of the indices are contested. Their case rests on the field-creating contribution: new cross-country data on investor protection and ownership, a clear framing, and 25–30 years of replication and critique. Differences in emphasis: Friberg states moderate confidence and concedes B001 does not compete on identification strength. Hassler and Strömberg would word the citation around measurable institutions and established empirical regularities, not the strong causal reading of legal origin. Hassler calls the gap with B048 small. Citation wordings differ slightly (programme, empirical field, or empirical findings). The chair is among these three supporters, which readers should weigh when reading this summary.

One file (Krusell) prefers B037, crediting Kiyotaki, Moore and Gertler for collateral constraints, credit cycles and the financial accelerator, with B048 and B040 as alternatives. He says Kiyotaki and Moore are the unambiguous core and would accept a two-name version if colleagues judge Gertler's credit too entangled with B040. Hassler, who proposes only Kiyotaki and Moore, lists B037 as an alternative but does not prefer it, and Dreber and Teorell also list it as an alternative. This position differs from B048 and B001 in both discovery and laureates. The stated reservations are overlap with the 2022 prize, Gertler's split credit with the New Keynesian entry, Gilchrist's exclusion, and weaker empirical identification of collateral channels than of the theory.

areas_of_agreement: Every round-1 file calls Melitz the identifiable originator in B048 and Helpman the natural second name. No file proposes Redding as a third name; those who address him treat his quantitative and spatial work as a later, separable strand.

Members across all three camps accept that B001's causal legal-origins claim and the coding of the investor-protection indices are contested, and that omitting Vishny under the three-name cap is a genuine attribution cost. They differ on how much this weighs against B001's field-creating role.

Several members (Dreber, Enflo, Fredriksson, Hjalmarsson) say that an earlier prize in trade (2008) or recent prizes in other themes bear on field balance or timing, not on scientific merit. No file argues that this should count as evidence against any candidate's merit.
Kiyotaki and Moore are described by Krusell, Hassler and Dreber as the clean core of B037.

B015 is rated highly on identification by several members, but multiple members (Boppart, Fredriksson, Friberg, Hjalmarsson, Strömberg, Andersson) find its three-name credit hard to define, because of the Katz-versus-Dorn choice and the task-framework lineage outside the ballot.
Members state that their assessments rest on their own knowledge of the literature and are not independently verified.
scientific_disputes: B001: whether the legal-origins thesis is a discovery or a contested hypothesis. Dreber, Enflo, Boppart, Fredriksson, Hjalmarsson, Krusell and Teorell stress endogeneity of legal origin, coding of the anti-director index, and the possibility that legal origin proxies for history or colonial experience. Hassler, Strömberg and Friberg argue that the lasting contribution is the data, the research design and the established regularities, which survive even if the causal story is only partly right.

Influence versus robustness: the B001 supporters weight reach and the research programme it created, while B048 supporters weight how well core predictions have survived testing. Friberg concedes B001 would not compete on identification credibility alone.

B048: members agree the qualitative predictions have held up, but note that welfare-gain magnitudes depend on functional-form assumptions such as Pareto productivity. Teorell relays Strömberg's earlier view that some empirical support is only partial.

B037: whether collateral-channel mechanisms are empirically identified well enough, versus being influential mainly as a conceptual and modelling contribution, and whether the 2022 prize reduces the marginal case.
B015: the size and persistence of the China-shock effects are described as still debated by several members.
attribution_disputes: B048: Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum (and Yeaple) developed parallel firm-level facts and models but are not on the ballot entry, so a Melitz-Helpman credit could be read as under-crediting empirical foundations. Hjalmarsson calls this the real vulnerability because it concerns priority. Several members propose wording the citation around the selection and reallocation mechanism.

B048: Helpman also appears in another candidate package (B026, trade politics). Andersson, Boppart, Dreber, Fredriksson, Hjalmarsson and Teorell raise this, and it is unresolved how it affects framing or support.

B001: the three-name cap excludes Vishny, a co-author of the core papers. Shleifer's wider work (limits to arbitrage, behavioural finance, privatisation) blurs the boundary of a citation limited to law and finance.

B037: Krusell would credit Kiyotaki, Moore and Gertler, while Hassler would credit Kiyotaki and Moore only. Gertler's record is split with B040, the accelerator lineage overlaps with Bernanke (2022), and Gilchrist is excluded.

B015: choice between Katz (skill-demand strand) and Dorn (China-shock papers), and the task-framework lineage involving Acemoglu, Levy and Murnane. Dreber's narrower two-name credit (Autor, Hanson) leaves out the technology strand.

B049 (alternative for several members): Strömberg would credit only Persson and Tabellini, treating Besley's state-capacity work as a distinct programme. Enflo asks whether the committee sees the constitutions work and Besley's work as one achievement or two.
maturity_disputes: B048 and B001: both are over 20 years old and are described by their supporters as mature. Friberg argues that the critiques of B001 are themselves evidence of maturity, while Dreber and others argue maturity should be judged by how well the central claims survived.
B037: the core papers are close to 30 years old and had a real-world test in 2008. The dispute is thematic overlap with the 2022 prize, not age.

B015: Fredriksson describes the core China-shock papers as about a decade old and rejects a maturity objection. Hjalmarsson and Boppart point instead to unsettled persistence and thematic overlap with the 2023 and 2024 labour and technology prizes.

B049 and B001: Andersson, Enflo and Strömberg raise thematic overlap with the 2024 institutions prize as affecting novelty at the margin. Members disagree on whether this is a merit argument or a timing argument.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Chair Hassler is one of three explicit B001 supporters. He discloses co-authorship and institutional ties with Krusell (B037 supporter, IIES), Boppart and Friberg, and none with credited names on B001, B048 or B037.
Krusell (B037 supporter) discloses co-authorship with Boppart and Hassler, and macroeconomics proximity to B037; he reports no tie to Kiyotaki, Moore, Gertler or Gilchrist.

Friberg discloses that his spouse is Magdalena Andersson, a Swedish politician, with no apparent bearing on these candidates. He also discloses co-authorship with Hassler and Ellingsen, and an industrial-organisation and trade field adjacent to B048.
Teorell discloses co-authorship with Torsten Persson (credited on B049, which he does not propose) and Stockholm University colleagues Hassler, Krusell and Boppart.
Boppart discloses a long-running collaboration with Peter Klenow (credited on B007, not in his configuration) and IIES colleagues, the chair and the secretary.
Strömberg discloses an adjunct post at Chicago Booth and a corporate-finance field close to B001, which he prefers.
Enflo discloses research proximity to Redding's spatial work (kept out of her credit), a past co-author link to Johannes Lindvall (no candidate connected), and Tommy Andersson's affiliation at Lund.
Fredriksson discloses labour-economics proximity to B015 (an alternative for him) and possible field bias. Hjalmarsson discloses possible familiarity bias toward empirical-design arguments.

Strömberg, Krusell, Hassler and Friberg mention possible reputational or conduct controversies around individuals associated with B001. No such evidence is documented in the permitted materials, and none of the files treats it as part of the merit case.
Conflicts are disclosed here and not adjudicated.
questions_for_round2: For B048 supporters: if the committee judges the Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum priority question material, would a citation limited to the selection and reallocation mechanism (as Hjalmarsson, Fredriksson and Dreber propose) suffice? Or would it change your preference between B048 and alternatives such as B001 or B015?

For B001 supporters (Friberg, Hassler, Strömberg): which specific claims in the law-and-finance record do you consider established despite the identification and coding critiques? Can you propose citation wording that avoids endorsing the strong causal legal-origins reading, and would B048 supporters find that wording sufficient?

For the six B048 supporters who list B001 as an alternative: head to head, which would you prefer if the committee accepted a citation resting on the data and research design, and what would change that ordering?

For Krusell and Hassler on B037: is the 2022 prize overlap disqualifying or only a reduction in marginal novelty, and is Gertler's inclusion essential or would a two-name Kiyotaki-Moore prize be acceptable? If the committee cannot settle this, would either of you move to B048 or B001?
Does Helpman's appearance on B026 affect his claim on B048, and should the committee treat it as a reason to define the B048 citation tightly or as an unresolved competing-claim issue?

Which of the following should the committee treat as evidence in comparing candidates: (a) thematic overlap with the 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025 prizes, (b) the 2008 trade prize, and (c) field rotation? Or should the comparison rest only on discovery, attribution and maturity?

Whom among B015's contributors would those who rank it highly (Fredriksson, Boppart, Hjalmarsson, Dreber) credit with three names, and is there a coherent citation that does not overlap with the 2023 and 2024 prizes?
summary.chair_observation: On explicit round-1 files, seven members prefer B048 (Melitz, Helpman), three prefer B001 (Shleifer, La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes) and one prefers B037 (Kiyotaki, Moore, Gertler). Four B048 supporters (Andersson, Boppart, Fredriksson, Hjalmarsson) state that they moved from other opening first choices, so these round-1 preferences are not the same as the opening rankings. All four members who do not prefer B048 list it as an alternative, and six of the seven B048 supporters list B001 as an alternative, so the two leading proposals are the main contest for round 2. The disagreement is mostly about what counts as discovery and robustness (field-creating influence versus tested core predictions) and about attribution (Vishny in B001; Bernard, Eaton, Jensen, Kortum and Helpman's other package in B048), not about whether either body of work is important. This summary reports stated positions only and makes no inference about hidden votes or nomination frequency. All assessments rest on members' own recollection of the literature and have not been independently verified. The chair's own B001 preference is included in the count and is disclosed.
